Container.Name: qbittorrentvpn
Container.Overview:
qBittorrent-nox with built-in WireGuard or OpenVPN client and an iptables killswitch that drops all non-VPN traffic if the tunnel goes down.
**VPN config:** - WireGuard: drop your provider's config into /config/wireguard/wg0.conf (filename must be exactly wg0.conf). - OpenVPN: drop your provider's .ovpn (or .conf) into /config/openvpn/. Set Steam-style credentials below — they are written to tmpfs at runtime so the plaintext password never touches the appdata volume.
**LAN_NETWORK** must contain your LAN's CIDR (e.g. 192.168.1.0/24) or the WebUI will be firewalled off from your LAN by the killswitch. Add the Docker bridge range (172.17.0.0/16) is NOT needed — handled internally.
**WireGuard IPv6** is auto-enabled in the container's network namespace when wg0.conf contains IPv6 addresses — no --sysctl flag needed on the run command.
**Kernel modules:** Requires tun.ko on the host. If wireguard.ko is missing, the container falls back to userspace wireguard-go automatically.
**WebUI login:** Set `WebUI Password` below (recommended) and the container will apply it on startup as admin (or whatever you set `WebUI Username` to). If you leave it empty, qBittorrent generates a one-time random password on first launch — find it in /config/qBittorrent/data/logs/qbittorrent.log inside the container.
**Ports:** 8080/tcp WebUI, 8999/tcp + 8999/udp BitTorrent listening.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: qBittorrent, WireGuard (/config/wireguard/wg0.conf), and OpenVPN (/config/openvpn/*.ovpn) config files.

Config.Name: Downloads
Config.Description: Default save path for torrents.

Config.Name: VPN Enabled
Config.Description: Enable the VPN client and iptables killswitch (yes/no). Disabling exposes your real IP — only set to 'no' if you know what you're doing.

Config.Name: VPN Type
Config.Description: wireguard or openvpn. WireGuard is recommended (faster, simpler config).

Config.Name: LAN Network
Config.Description: Comma-separated CIDR ranges for your LAN(s), e.g. 192.168.1.0/24,10.0.0.0/24. Required so the killswitch lets the WebUI through to your LAN.

Config.Name: OpenVPN Username
Config.Description: OpenVPN account username. Leave empty for WireGuard. Written to a tmpfs file at runtime — never persisted to /config.

Config.Name: OpenVPN Password
Config.Description: OpenVPN account password. Leave empty for WireGuard. Written to a tmpfs file at runtime — never persisted to /config.

Config.Name: WebUI Username
Config.Description: qBittorrent WebUI login username. Only takes effect when WebUI Password is also set.

Config.Name: WebUI Password
Config.Description: qBittorrent WebUI login password. When set, the container hashes it with PBKDF2 and writes it into qBittorrent's config on every start. Leave empty to let qBittorrent generate a one-time random password on first launch (check qBittorrent's log file under /config/qBittorrent/data/logs/ for the value).

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID applied to /config files and /downloads. Unraid default: 99 (nobody).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID applied to /config files and /downloads. Unraid default: 100 (users).

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: Umask for files created by qBittorrent.

Config.Name: Health Check Host
Config.Description: Host pinged by the in-container health loop to verify VPN connectivity. Hostname tests DNS too; an IP only tests raw connectivity.

Config.Name: Health Check Interval
Config.Description: Seconds between in-container health pings.

Config.Name: Health Check Amount
Config.Description: Number of pings sent per health check.

Config.Name: Health Check Silent
Config.Description: 1 = suppress 'Network is up' log lines on every check; 0 = log every check.

Config.Name: Restart on Network Failure
Config.Description: Exit the container when the health check fails so Docker restarts it. Set 'no' to keep the container running for debugging.

Config.Name: VPN Wait Timeout
Config.Description: Seconds to wait for the VPN tunnel interface to appear before giving up and exiting.

Config.Name: WebUI Listen Port (internal)
Config.Description: Port qBittorrent's WebUI listens on INSIDE the container. Leave at 8080 unless you have a specific reason to change it. If you change this, you MUST also change the 'Container Port' of the 'WebUI Port' port mapping below to the same value — otherwise the host port forwards to nothing.

Config.Name: Enable UPnP
Config.Description: UPnP port mapping in qBittorrent. Disabled by default — UPnP is ineffective behind a VPN and can leak.

Config.Name: Enable SSL
Config.Description: WebUI SSL handling: 'yes' generates a self-signed cert and enables HTTPS; 'no' strips SSL config; 'ignore' leaves your settings alone.

Config.Name: Name Servers
Config.Description: Comma-separated DNS servers. OpenVPN only — WireGuard uses the DNS= line in wg0.conf and ignores this.

Config.Name: Legacy iptables
Config.Description: Set 'yes' to use iptables-legacy instead of iptables-nft. Needed only on hosts running older kernels that don't speak nf_tables.

Config.Name: Additional Ports
Config.Description: Comma-separated TCP ports to open through the killswitch (e.g. 8112,1234) for linked containers like Sonarr/Radarr.

Config.Name: Skip chown on /downloads
Config.Description: Set 'yes' to skip the recursive chown on /downloads at startup. Useful for large libraries where the chown adds minutes to startup.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: WebUI port. The HOST PORT (left field) is what you'll use in your browser. The CONTAINER PORT (right field) must match the 'WebUI Listen Port' variable in advanced settings — if you didn't change that variable, leave the container port at 8080.

Config.Name: BitTorrent Port (TCP)
Config.Description: qBittorrent peer listening port (TCP).

Config.Name: BitTorrent Port (UDP)
Config.Description: qBittorrent peer listening port (UDP) — used by DHT, uTP, and UDP trackers.
